identity.name: assert_schema
identity.description: CQA Tier 1 pre-ingestion schema validation: CKAN field sets for permits/CoA/zoning, CSV headers for address points and parcels, GeoJSON property keys for neighbourhoods, and URL reachability for the shapefile archives.

why_lock.text: Shared across specs 41/42/43, so no single spec number identifies it; 102 was assigned from the Spec 47 §A.5 next-free registry.

on_check_error_why.text: Fold A correction 4. Eight of the nine checks already fail the step when their own fetch throws: the per-source catch sets allPassed=false and the circuit breaker halts the chain. fail_step is therefore the POLICY. The single omit — a non-OK sample fetch inside validateTypeSample returning true — is a per-check limitation, recorded under limitations[] against permit_cost_type_sample, not a step-wide error policy.

why.text: RULING R-D (2026-08-28) — cloud parity is a chain-start assertion. A step whose descriptor declares a config.logic_variables[] name with no logic_variables ROW throws LM-D15's mid-chain error (scripts/lib/step/config.js resolveConfig) — correct, but discovered however many steps deep into the chain that step happens to sit, after every step ahead of it already ran. assert_schema is step 1 of every chain that runs it, so probing the SAME registry here turns a mid-chain throw into a minute-zero FAIL naming the exact remedy. `expect` is the STATIC union of every scripts/steps/_schema/converted.json step's config.logic_variables[].name at authoring time (Spec 122 P1/P2 — a compute may not read the filesystem, so this is DECLARED data, not scanned); the SAME list is declared as `config.probe_presence`, which is what the library actually queries (claim #175 — the compute issues no SQL, so the presence read happens in scripts/lib/step/config.js resolveConfig, not here, and the compute only observes ctx.probePresence). src/tests/steps/assert_schema/ locks `expect` === `config.probe_presence` === the live scripts/lib/declared-logic-variables.js derivation, so none of the three can drift from the other two. Narrowed (not chain-start-universal): entities/wsib/deep_scrapes run no assert_schema at all — LM-D15's mid-step throw is the sole backstop there until a WF adds assert_schema to them (followup filed).
Allowing downstream scripts to run against a drifted permit schema would silently corrupt 240K+ permit records.

CKAN injects sentinel rows and comma-formatted numbers; a type flip to unparseable text would zero out every cost estimate downstream. blocking:true states what the code does today — a failed sample sets allPassed=false and reaches the circuit breaker — and the schema's allOf then forces when:"pre".
WARD is text in the CoA Active resource and WARD_NUMBER is int4 in Closed; only the Active set is validated here because only Active is fetched pre-ingestion.
Address Points became the canonical source for ADDRESS_NUMBER and LINEAR_NAME_FULL when Toronto stripped them from the Property Boundaries CSV on 2026-05-20.

An OR-contract, not a flat column requirement: the live CSV ships a geometry GeoJSON column and LAT/LONG are the fallback. The real loss mode is neither being present, which yields a 0-row spatial bridge. Fence 646ea5a7 — the OR is evaluated in the compute by hasCoordinateSource(); geometry/LATITUDE/LONGITUDE must NEVER re-enter address_point_columns.expect as flat required columns.

Parcels feeds all three chains (link_parcels in permits, link_coa_to_parcels in coa, and the sources loaders), so its drift rows are emitted into every chain's audit table per Spec 79 CRIT-3a. Peel 8a retired the constant-zero fiction: the compute no longer reads the chain, so wherever this check is SELECTED the parcels CSV header is actually fetched and the row reports a measurement. The cost is one extra ranged GET (bytes=0-2048) on the permits and coa chains; the gain is that a permits-chain parcels drift is no longer invisible.

These resources have datastore_active=false, so no field-set check is possible pre-download; attribute presence is validated post-download inside each loader. Reachability is the only pre-flight signal available. Fences 1ceebd17 (ravine_zip) and f6047e89 (centreline_zip) are carried by this subject set together with inputs.reads.externals.
The neighbourhoods GeoJSON upsert key is the ID property; losing both spellings would key every neighbourhood to null.

Pre-flight reachability plus upsert-key and geometry presence over 10 DataStore resources; full attribute drift is enforced at load time by zoning-attr-drift.js. Fold A correction 2 and fence 58914fa8: the code has THREE distinct required sets, not two — base (6 columns), the height overlay's HT_LABEL and the lot-coverage overlay's PRCNT_CVER — so expect is a per-resource map keyed by CKAN resource id.

deviations.from: Spec 122 §8.2's pilot table, which assigns assert_schema write class L (verdict_only)

why.text: The standalone pipeline_runs INSERT and UPDATE are the RUNNER's ledger row, not a step output; claim #39 consolidates ledger ownership into the library, so post-conversion this step writes nothing and outputs is "none" as the ASSERT profile requires.

deviations.from: the live emission records_total: 0 at assert-schema.js:571

why.text: §1.10 forces an ASSERT to declare counters "none". Spec 122 §12.5 records that 0 of 5 ASSERTs comply today, so this profile is NORMATIVE, not descriptive; the differential at conversion must show the counter emission moving to the runner rather than changing value silently.

241 had no basis — it is fix_lead_id_trigger_column_scope, which this step never touches. The only table this step reads or writes is pipeline_runs (created by 033); the library writes records_meta (finalizeLedgerRow), a column added by migration 041, and pipeline.run applies no floor of its own, so 41 is the real floor (OUTPUT-panel grounder, 2026-08-25; earlier 33 under-counted). The database object admits no why field (additionalProperties:false), so the justification is recorded here

deviations.from: the draft descriptor's two distinct failed terminals, fail_check (schema_drift_detected) and fail_error (fetch_error)

why.text: Both are one throw in the code — the circuit breaker — so nothing observable distinguishes them and a two-terminal declaration would be a fiction. Fold B merged them at commit 7; the fetch-path liveness handle is carried onto the survivor rather than lost. RE-EXAMINED AT PEEL 8b AND LEFT MERGED: check-id attribution now distinguishes the two CAUSES inside the audit table (an errored check renders as `check errored: <msg>` while a violated one renders its violation count), but `terminals[]` has no runtime consumer anywhere in the library — `grep -rn terminals scripts/lib/` returns 0 — so the runner selects no terminal and a second declared terminal would still be a fiction. Splitting them needs the terminal-selection wave, not another compute peel.

deviations.from: the §1.2a P4 standard posture on_invalid: "fail" for a declared logic variable

why.text: These three vars are seeded by the mig-099 seed contract (scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json applied at the END of npm run migrate), NOT by a migration, so every DB that has not re-run the seed lacks the rows. Under "fail" the config resolver would REFUSE this step on those DBs — a pre-ingestion gate that halts three chains because a knob was externalized. Under "default" the resolver falls back to the seed default, which the parity lock pins byte-equal to the pre-externalization literal (20 / 2048 / 8192), so behaviour is IDENTICAL pre-seed and the only cost is that an out-of-bounds operator edit degrades loudly (a pipeline.log.warn naming the raw value, the bound and the substituted default) instead of halting. "fail" is the standard for a variable with no safe default; each of these has one, and it is the value the step ran on for its entire history. The config object admits no per-variable why field (additionalProperties:false), so the justification is recorded here.

deviations.adjudicated_by: Spec 122 §1.2a P4 / Pilot 1 P4 remediation plan

limitations.what: A non-OK HTTP response inside validateTypeSample returns true, so the permit cost-type check cannot distinguish 'verified' from 'never ran'.
limitations.measured: scripts/lib/compute/assert-schema.js — `if (!res.ok) return true; // non-fatal` inside validateTypeSample (ported verbatim from assert-schema.js:163)

limitations.what: Shapefile and ZIP sources are checked for reachability only; their attribute contracts are enforced post-download inside each loader, so a reachable-but-drifted archive passes this step.
limitations.measured: assert-schema.js:365-404 — five checkUrlAccessible calls, no attribute inspection

limitations.what: checks_passed and errors have NO reader anywhere in the estate, and checks_failed's one reader is effectively dead: FreshnessTimeline.tsx renders it only on the branch where records_meta carries no audit_table, which the step library always populates. They are emitted for continuity with the pre-conversion payload, not because anything consumes them — the earlier consumer list naming run-chain.js and /api/quality was false.
limitations.measured: grep -rn 'checks_passed|checks_failed' over src/ and scripts/run-chain.js, 2026-08-25 — zero matches in run-chain.js and src/app/api/quality/; one match at src/components/FreshnessTimeline.tsx:1092

limitations.what: The coordinate-source OR-contract (geometry OR LATITUDE+LONGITUDE) cannot be expressed by any limit form the schema offers, so its rule lives as prose here and as logic in the compute's hasCoordinateSource() call; the descriptor states the contract, the check id carries it, and the fence lock proves both directions.
limitations.measured: scripts/lib/compute/assert-schema.js — one hasCoordinateSource(new Set(apHeaders)) call site; assert-schema.js:339 pre-conversion

why.text: pipeline.js emits PIPELINE_SUMMARY with records_meta {skipped:true, reason:'advisory_lock_held_elsewhere'} because assert-schema passes no opts to withAdvisoryLock. Contention IS observable today; what was missing is a declared policy.

Schema drift must halt the chain — the step throws after emitting, so the audit table is recorded before the failure propagates. Fold B merged fail_error into this terminal: a CKAN metadata fetch or CSV range request that throws is caught per-source, reddens its own audit row and reaches the SAME circuit-breaker throw, so the two exit paths are indistinguishable in the code and declaring them separately would be a fiction. The fetch path's liveness handle is carried here.
